Blended CPA for 2025 was about **$1,315.65 per closed-won deal**. That is $13,905,118.46 in total marketing spend divided by 10,569 closed-won deals.

- **Spend:** I summed these sources over the weeks starting 2025-01-06 through 2025-12-22:

  | Source | 2025 spend (USD) |
  |---|---|
  | Google | 7,938,164.71 |
  | Display | 1,810,522.73 |
  | Meta | 1,104,166.56 |
  | LinkedIn | 1,002,729.19 |
  | CTV | 757,255.90 |
  | Partner fees | 756,335.13 |
  | Webinars | 535,944.24 |

  Webinars are counted by event date, since they have no weekly figure. Email has no cost data, so it isn't included.
- **Deals:** I counted opportunities with stage "Closed Won" and a 2025 close date. There were no duplicate opportunity IDs.

"Blended CPA" isn't defined in the data, so I took it to mean all paid spend over all closed-won deals. A narrower definition, such as ad platforms only, would give a lower figure.

I can't give you a true incremental CPA for Connected TV in 2025. The data doesn't contain what that would need.

- **No lift measurement:** None of the tables has a geo holdout, lift test, or conversion-lift result. `ctv_weekly` only has spend, impressions, completed views and `attributed_leads`, which are platform-attributed. Incremental CPA needs a counterfactual: what leads would have come without CTV.
- **No agreed method:** CTV runs in only 8 regions, and some weeks are missing in each. I could try to build a quasi-experiment from that, or model it against `crm_leads` and `fleet_activity_index_weekly`. But the result would depend on assumptions I don't have a definition for, such as which regions count as controls and how to handle seasonality and overlap with other channels. That would be an estimate, not a measured figure.
- **Budget changes confound it:** `media_plan_changes` shows CTV budget moves, and other channels were adjusted at the same times.

I can give you the attributed CPA for 2025 instead. It uses the platform-attributed leads, so it is not incremental. Total spend is about $757K and attributed leads are about 9,177, which gives roughly $82.5 per lead. That is a cost per lead, not a cost per acquisition. I can also run a geo-based incrementality model if you give me the method and control definition to use.

Display retargeting's cost per platform-reported conversion in 2024 was about $89.65.

- **Spend:** $1,478,601.54 in media cost, from `ads_display_weekly`. I used the 52 weeks whose Monday falls in 2024, from 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-23. The week of 2024-12-30 counts toward 2025.
- **Conversions:** 16,493, which is 2,484 post-click plus 14,009 post-view.
- **Cost per conversion:** $1,478,601.54 ÷ 16,493 ≈ $89.65.

Two assumptions:
- The display table has no campaign column. I treated all of it as retargeting because the CRM's only display campaign is tagged "retargeting".
- I counted both post-click and post-view conversions as platform-reported. Counting post-click only would give about $595 per conversion.

I can't give a blended CPA for 2023, because the data doesn't define two things the number depends on.

- **What counts as an acquisition.** Several candidates exist and they give very different answers:
  - Closed Won opportunities in `crm_opportunities`.
  - Leads, MQLs or SQLs in `crm_leads`.
  - Platform-reported conversions. These aren't comparable across channels: Google counts "conversions", LinkedIn counts "conversions", Meta counts "leads", display splits post-click from post-view, and CTV counts "attributed_leads".
- **Which costs go into "blended".** The data has paid media spend (Google, LinkedIn, Meta, display, CTV). It also has partner fees and webinar costs. Email has no cost field, and there is no data on headcount or tooling costs. I don't know which of these your definition includes.

Any figure I picked would be an estimate based on my own assumptions, not Fernhook's definition. If you tell me the numerator (which cost sources) and the denominator (for example, Closed Won deals by close date in 2023), I'll calculate it.

Last-touch cost per lead for brand paid search in 2025 was about $58.64. That is $2,493,236.59 of spend divided by 42,519 leads.

- **Leads:** I counted `crm_leads` rows created in 2025 with source `google`, medium `cpc` and campaign `search_brand`. I matched these case-insensitively, because the source has both `google` and `Google` variants.
- **Last-touch assumption:** The UTM fields on each lead are the only attribution I have, so I treated them as the last touch. The data has no separate touch history to check that against.

YouTube's last-touch CPA in 2024 was about **$14,582**, counting a closed-won opportunity as an acquisition.

- **Spend:** I used the Google Ads video campaign, `FH_YouTube_Prospecting`. Its 2024 cost was $597,880.14. This is the only YouTube spend in the data.
- **Last-touch acquisitions:** I counted CRM leads whose `utm_source` is YouTube (any capitalization) and that have a Closed Won opportunity. There were 41 in 2024. The count is 41 whether I date them by lead creation or by close date.
- **CPA:** $597,880.14 ÷ 41 = $14,582.44.

The data has no definition of "acquisition", so the closed-won choice is my assumption. If you meant leads instead, the 2024 figure would be about $762.60 on 784 leads.

Affiliate last-touch ROAS for 2025 was about 2.27. That means roughly $2.27 of closed-won revenue for every $1 of affiliate spend.

- **Revenue:** $1,715,680. This is the sum of Closed Won opportunity amounts with a 2025 close date. I counted a deal as affiliate when its lead has `utm_medium = affiliate`, which covers `partner_network` and `reseller` in every casing variant. I treated the lead's UTM as its last touch, because the CRM holds no separate touch history.
- **Spend:** $756,335.13. This is `partner_fees` from `partners_weekly` for the 51 weeks whose Monday falls in 2025 (Jan 6 to Dec 22, all 20 regions). I assumed partner fees are the full cost of the affiliate channel.

LinkedIn generated about $2.84 of pipeline per dollar of spend in 2023 on a last-touch basis.

- **Pipeline:** $5,235,720. This is the total amount of all opportunities created in 2023 (open, won and lost) whose lead's `utm_source` is LinkedIn. I matched "linkedin" and "LinkedIn" together.
- **Spend:** $1,845,078.64. This is LinkedIn `cost_usd` summed over the 52 weeks starting 2023-01-02 through 2023-12-25.
- **Ratio:** 5,235,720 / 1,845,078.64 ≈ 2.84.

I had no official definition of "pipeline", so I counted every opportunity amount regardless of stage. I also treated the lead's `utm_source` as the last touch, since that is the only attribution field in the data. If you define pipeline as open opportunities only, or as closed-won only, the figure will be lower.

Partners (the affiliate channel) had the lowest last-touch CPA in 2025, at about $1,403 per closed-won deal. That is $756,335 of partner fees divided by 539 closed-won deals.

I attributed each closed-won deal (closed in 2025) to the UTM source and medium on its lead. Spend is 2025 weekly spend, with weeks assigned by their Monday. Some UTM values differ only by capitalization, so I matched them case-insensitively.

| Channel | 2025 spend | Closed-won deals | CPA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Partners / affiliate (partner_network, reseller) | $756,335 | 539 | ~$1,403 |
| Google search (cpc) | $7,589,990 | 3,685 | ~$2,060 |
| Meta (Facebook and Instagram paid social) | $1,104,167 | 419 | ~$2,635 |
| LinkedIn | $1,002,729 | 330 | ~$3,039 |
| Display (dsp, programmatic) | $1,810,523 | 302 | ~$5,995 |
| YouTube / Google video | $348,174 | 27 | ~$12,895 |

Two judgment calls shape this result:
- **Partners as paid:** I counted partner fees as paid spend. If affiliate doesn't count as a paid channel, Google search is lowest at about $2,060.
- **CTV excluded:** CTV has spend but no matching UTM source on leads, so it has no last-touch deals and drops out.

Combined last-touch cost per lead for brand and non-brand paid search in 2024 was about **$82.32**.

- **Spend:** I summed Google Ads spend for the two search campaigns, `FH_Search_Brand` and `FH_Search_NonBrand`, over weeks starting in 2024. That comes to $6,473,459.20. I left out the YouTube campaign.
- **Leads:** I counted CRM leads created in 2024 with source Google, medium cpc, and campaign `search_brand` or `search_nonbrand`. That comes to 78,633. The CRM spells the source "google" and "Google" both, so I matched them case-insensitively.
- **Calculation:** $6,473,459.20 ÷ 78,633 = $82.32.

I treated each lead's recorded UTM source as its last touch. The data has no separate attribution field.

I can't answer this from the available data, because there's no definition of customer lifetime value and nothing to build one from.

- **No retention data:** There are no tables for churn, renewals, subscriptions, contract length or recurring revenue. The only revenue-like field is `crm_opportunities.amount`, which is a deal amount at close. It doesn't show how long a customer stays or what they pay over time.
- **No margin data:** I can't convert revenue to a profit-based lifetime value.
- **No agreed formula:** Lifetime value could mean average deal size, ARPA divided by churn, or a margin-adjusted figure. I don't have the definition Fernhook uses.

I could give you the average closed-won deal amount for paid search leads (`utm_medium` = cpc or similar). That is first-deal value, not lifetime value. If you give me a lifetime or churn assumption, or confirm that first-deal value is what you want, I'll calculate it.
